result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A tells the dispatcher to cover the Meaning column and drill in random order, so the sheet works as a signal-to-meaning self-test. Its grouping boxes add extra material, shorten some meanings ('Backup', 'Medical') and show the answers below the table, which weakens the cover-up test. B is a clean, faithful and very readable table, but nothing visible in it supports testing from memory, so it is only a reference list. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both sheets list all ten signals with the exact meanings, in clean, legible tables. B adds a short instruction to cover the Meaning column and test yourself, so it supports signal-to-meaning recall. It loses points because its grouping boxes repeat shortened meanings (e.g. 'M-4 Backup') that stay visible when the column is covered, and it adds some extra material. A is a plain reference table with no visible way to test recall, and its screenshot is cut off at an unexplained box at the bottom.
